subject: Post-call: Model fit & eval next steps (PayGrid)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & eval next steps (PayGrid)

Hi Alex — great to meet you and the PayGrid ML team this morning. Thanks for walking through the three priority inference workloads (transaction categorization, dispute triage, and reconciliation summarization). This note captures the next steps we agreed on and our recommended starting eval plan so we can quickly measure parity vs your in-house baseline.

Recap / immediate asks:
- You’ll share the minimal sample prompt set & golden labels for ~200 examples per workload (we discussed stratifying by high/medium/low complexity).
- Redwood will run a 1-day model-fit eval across the following candidate models and return per-workload metrics:
  - Open models: Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized), Mistral-7B-v2, Falcon-40B-instruct (fp16 where possible)
  - Lightweight suggestion for latency-sensitive paths: Mistral/Mistral quantized or Redwood-optimized 13B variant
- We’ll compare against the PayGrid baseline (you noted an internal 'PayGridBase-3B' classifier/seq2seq) and report accuracy, precision/recall, latency P50/P95, and cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Deliverables by next Tue (2026-07-14): summary spreadsheet, per-example failure cases, and a recommended model+config per workload + a short mutual action plan.

Immediate blockers / risks we flagged:
- Quality regression acceptance: you mentioned a tolerance of up to 3% absolute accuracy drop if latency/cost improvements are >2x. We’ll mark that as an acceptance threshold but will call out any semantic regressions in triage flows.
- Data sensitivity: we discussed redaction before upload; please confirm whether the sample set needs additional masking.

Attachments I’m sending with this thread: prompt set template + initial benchmark harness (see attached JSONL + CSV stub). If you can drop the sample labels in the Drive link below, we’ll kick off the run.

Thanks — I’ll own the eval run and loop you in with results.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- paygrid-eval-promptset-v1.jsonl (prompt templates + example metadata)
- mutual-action-plan-paygrid.pdf (timeline & responsibilities)
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ML Team <ml@paygrid.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & eval next steps (PayGrid)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and for putting the plan together so quickly. Confirming a few items from our side: 

- We’ll sanitize and upload the three 200-example sets by EOD tomorrow (2026-07-13). We’ll keep the original labels in a separate file and provide the redacted versions for the public eval runs.
- Acceptance threshold: agreed that up to 3% absolute accuracy drop is tolerable if we get >=2x latency or cost improvements; for dispute triage we may have a tighter threshold and will flag that in the labels sheet.
- Please prioritize the transaction categorization workload — that’s our highest volume and will drive the most savings.

Also — curious on the recommended prompt engineering baseline. We run a short retrieval step + prompt prefix; happy for Redwood to try both with and without our retriever to isolate model quality vs retrieval impact.

I’ll upload the data to the Drive link and update the HubSpot deal with the MLP contact details. Looking forward to the results.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Head of ML Engineering, PayGrid
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & eval next steps (PayGrid)

Looping in with a short tech plan for the eval run. Marissa — I’ll take the execution and share intermediate results by EOD Monday.

Execution notes:
- Models to run (initial sweep): Llama-2-13B-chat (ggml quant), Mistral-7B-v2 (int8), Falcon-40B-instruct (fp16). If PayGrid uploads retrieval artifacts, we’ll run both Retriever+Prompt and Prompt-only paths.
- Metrics: accuracy/F1 per-class, latency (P50/P95) on a t4-small-equivalent baseline, tokenized cost estimate (using our cost model). We’ll also produce an examples.csv with per-example outputs for side-by-side parity inspection.
- Parity checks: we’ll compute delta vs PayGridBase-3B on (1) accuracy, (2) top-1 label match, and (3) semantic similarity for open-ended summarization (using a small annotated set).
- Regression alert rule: any example where the model's label differs from golden and the semantic similarity falls below 0.75 will be flagged as a potential regression and manually triaged.
- Run time: expect initial sweep ~3–5 hrs once samples are available; we’ll push a lightweight dashboard link to the Drive summary.

Aditya — can you provision a short-lived batch on Dedicated for the Falcon-40B run? Keep it under the trial budget and notify me when ready.

Marissa — I’ll include the per-workload recommendation (model + quantization + batching config) in the Monday deliverable.

—Rishi
Sr. Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@paygrid.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & eval next steps (PayGrid)

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround, Alex. Please ping here once the Drive upload is complete and include a sample file name so Rishi can pick it up.

As a reminder on our end: we’ll prioritize transaction categorization and send the initial results + recommended config by Tue (2026-07-14) morning PST. If PayGrid wants a tighter SLA on the Falcon run or more parity diagnostics, we can scope that as an add-on in the mutual action plan.

Cheers,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
